run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T01:19:41Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy itself records error spans: its 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR / http.status_code=503, and its paired 'router frontend egress' spans carry http.status_code=0, i.e. the upstream (frontend) never returned an HTTP response. Envoy access logs confirm '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward upstream 'frontend'. A low rate of these 503s exists from the first available sample (~00:49) onward, and the alert-time deviation is a burst at ~01:11-01:16 (33-78 error spans/5m vs 1-5 before/after) in which frontend's own POST /api/checkout -> grpc CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans errored and checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge was rejected instantly (all failed Charge spans <=2 ms versus healthy ones up to >2000 ms), while payment recorded no error status and only logged successful charges. The leading hypothesis is the fault-injection setting paymentUnreachable=on in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config ('Payment service is unavailable'), which matches the observed payment-unreachable failure path; however payment kept serving charges and checkout errors stopped at 01:17 although the flag still reads 'on', so the timing is not fully explained. An alternative candidate is the Deployment payment pod replacement at 01:10:03, the only cluster change in otel-demo during the window. The exact alert expression could not be read (no RequestErrorRate rule in the queried Prometheus), and recomputed error ratios do not reproduce the alert's 0.0222.

claims.text: frontend-proxy emitted error spans continuously from the first available sample (00:49/00:51) to 01:29: span 'ingress' status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR was ~1.1-4.4 per 5m in most buckets, jumped to 33.3 at 01:11 and 77.8 at 01:13 and 01:15, then fell back to ~1.25-4.8 by 01:19-01:29; span 'router frontend egress' errors mirror the same counts.

In a retained frontend-proxy error trace, the 'ingress' span has error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR and is the parent of a 'router frontend egress' span with error=true and http.status_code=0 (no HTTP response from the upstream); the calling load-generator GET span carries the same 503 ERROR status.

frontend-proxy container logs contain 503 lines with response flag 'UC' and response-code detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for upstream 'frontend', e.g. "GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP HTTP/1.1" 503 UC at 01:12:15 and "GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ HTTP/1.1" 503 UC at 01:15:31.

During the deviation the frontend service recorded its own errors only at the 01:12:41 and 01:14:41 buckets (306.67 per 5m, i.e. ~76.7 failed requests x 4 spans) on span names 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'; frontend error counts are 0 in all other buckets of the window.

The checkout service's error spans occur only on span names 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' (client) and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (server), with identical counts: 52.7 at 01:12:00, 46.8 at 01:13:00, 45.6 at 01:14:00, 44.3 at 01:15:00, 45.6 at 01:16:00 and 0 from 01:17:00 onward.

The failed checkout->payment Charge spans were immediate rejections, not timeouts: at 01:14:30 all error-status Charge spans fall in the lowest duration buckets (le=2.0 equals le=10.0 equals the +Inf total of 44.83), whereas all Charge spans without status filtering spread through the 200-2000 ms and 5000-10000 ms buckets (total 151.49).

The payment service recorded no error status at any time in 01:10-01:25: its spans 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' and 'charge' are STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while its Charge span rate dropped from ~212 per 5m at 01:10 to 125/90/123/110/133 per 5m at 01:12-01:16 and recovered to 211-224 per 5m by 01:21-01:25.

payment-54499f9786-4r25d container logs show only successful pairs of 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' during the burst and afterwards (continuously from 01:12:59 through 01:17:59, and 01:23:00-01:24:00), with no error lines.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) currently sets the fault-injection flag paymentUnreachable to defaultVariant 'on' with description 'Payment service is unavailable', while all other fault flags in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) are set to 'off'.

The payment Deployment was rolled out at 01:10:03-01:10:06: ScalingReplicaSet created/scaled payment-54499f9786 from 0 to 1 (pod scheduled 01:10:03, container created 01:10:05, started 01:10:06) and scaled payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0 with 'Killing' of pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 at 01:10:06; those 9 events are the only events recorded in namespace otel-demo in the window.

All 21 pods in otel-demo are Running and ready with restart counts of 0 at query time, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt (created 00:37:51), frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks (00:37:51), checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp (00:37:52) and payment-54499f9786-4r25d (01:10:03); no pod shows an Evicted condition, OOMKilled last termination or a non-zero exit code.

The payment Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, port 8080) matches the payment pod-template labels, and the payment Endpoints list payment-54499f9786-4r25d at 100.96.5.201:8080 as its only address; checkout's Deployment targets payment at PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and its env plus the frontend Deployment env contain no fault-injection variables.

The error rate the alert reports is not reproduced by simple ratios recomputed at 01:19:41: whole-service 5m error ratio = 0.00056, ingress-only 5m = 0.00112, ingress-only 10m = 0.0119, versus the alert annotation's 0.0222, and no RequestErrorRate alerting rule was returned by this Prometheus.

The paymentUnreachable=on explanation does not fit the timing on its own: payment completed charges throughout and after the burst and checkout Charge errors returned to 0 at 01:17 while the ConfigMap still reads paymentUnreachable 'on' at 01:37, so a continuously enabled boolean 'payment unavailable' flag cannot by itself explain a failure burst limited to ~01:11-01:16.

Rejected: that payment charges were failing inside the payment service (payment-side fault such as paymentFailure). payment spans carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET, its logs contain only successful 'Transaction complete.' lines and the paymentFailure flag reads 'off'; the failures exist only on checkout's client side as instant rejections.

Leading hypothesis: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config drives the deviation through its fault-injection flag paymentUnreachable=on ('Payment service is unavailable'). Its declared fault matches the observed failure path exactly - checkout's calls to oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge rejected instantly (<=2 ms) while payment records no server-side error - and it is the only fault-declaring setting found among the otel-demo ConfigMaps and the payment/checkout/frontend Deployment env vars that were read.

Alternative hypothesis: Deployment payment's pod replacement at 01:10:03-01:10:06 (old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 killed, new pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d started) left checkout's gRPC channel failing fast against a dead/stale payment endpoint until it converged at ~01:16:30, which would explain the <=2 ms rejections, the partial loss of Charge traffic at payment and the 5-minute duration. The trigger for that rollout is unknown (no change history available).

Second alternative hypothesis for the non-checkout share of the proxy errors: the sporadic 1-5 per 5m 503 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' responses on GET requests, which exist throughout the available baseline and never produce a frontend error span, may be keep-alive connection-termination races on frontend rather than application failures; this would make them background noise rather than part of the alerting deviation.

Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression and evaluation window) from the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that actually fired it, since the registered Prometheus returned no such rule and no recomputed ratio reproduces 0.0222; this is needed to state precisely which window the alert measured.

Retrieve change history for the otel-demo release around 01:10 UTC (who patched Deployment payment and whether otel-demo/flagd-config was changed in the same operation) and set paymentUnreachable back to 'off' if the payment-unavailable fault is not intended; verify recovery through checkout's PlaceOrder and frontend-proxy's ingress error rate. No change was made in this run.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what triggered the Deployment payment rollout at 01:10:03 and whether otel-demo/flagd-config was modified at the same time cannot be determined.

ConfigMap content is readable only as current state: flagd-config's paymentUnreachable value during 01:11-01:17 cannot be verified, and the flagd pod (flagd-678dcfdc67-bl78w) returned no readable log lines (status no_data), so no flag-change timestamp exists.

Jaeger no longer holds the burst's traces: queries for checkout over 01:11-01:18 and 01:24-01:35 returned no_data and the newest frontend-proxy trace sample observed was 01:02:57, so the checkout-side error message and status detail (connection refused vs deadline exceeded) could not be read.

The frontend container (frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt) returned zero readable log bytes for the incident window (status no_data), so the frontend application's own error text and any connection-abort reason are unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule does not exist in the queried Prometheus (rule_name and type=alert queries returned no_data), so the alert's expression, threshold and evaluation window are unknown and the reported 0.0222 could not be reproduced from traces_span_metrics_calls_total ratios.

The kube-state series kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and kube_pod_container_info returned no_data, so image digests of the old and new payment pods could not be compared to confirm whether the 01:10 rollout was configuration-only.
Reads of networkpolicies and resourcequotas returned no_data, so their absence in the cluster cannot be asserted and they cannot be excluded as a cause of connection refusals.

Frontend-proxy access-log evidence and metric evidence disagree in magnitude for the burst (roughly 78 error spans per 5m in metrics versus two '503 UC' access-log lines between 01:09 and 01:17), and this discrepancy is unresolved.
Only three representative workloads' Deployment env vars (payment, checkout, frontend) were inspected for fault-injection settings; the remaining otel-demo deployments were not read.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate rule from the firing Prometheus/Alertmanager to fix the exact evaluation window and confirm which error signal (metric, labels, aggregation) supplies 0.0222.
Review Helm/CI/audit change history for otel-demo around 2026-11-17T01:10Z covering Deployment payment and ConfigMap flagd-config.
Collect retained checkout logs or longer-retention traces for 01:11-01:17 to confirm whether the failed oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls were refused/unavailable versus injected failures.
If the paymentUnreachable fault is not intended, revert it to 'off' and confirm that checkout PlaceOrder errors and frontend-proxy ingress 503s stop.
Investigate the sporadic frontend-proxy 503 'UC connection_termination' background on GET requests separately, since it predates the deviation and keeps the error rate above zero.
